notes: READ THIS FILE BESIDE data/rounds/SCHEMA.md. Every field the schema documents appears above at least once, so the printed block is also a tour of what the synthesiser can check.

THE POINT OF THE FORMAT: the file supplies the QUESTIONS (which card, which scale, which target, which knob), and the ledger supplies the ANSWERS by re-reading the shipped data at run time. Nothing above is a number this receipt trusts — `before`/`after`/`movers`/`top12` are snapshots of the moment, and where the board has moved on, the block prints the drift as a SUPERSESSION rather than a failure.

WHAT WOULD FAIL, and should: the PIPELINE_VERSION floor, a knob pattern that no longer matches its file, the subject missing its target band, any `expect`, any `order`, and any named card that has left the pool (MISSING).

WHAT WOULD NOT FAIL: the subject drifting off its recorded `after`, a mover no longer sitting on its recorded value, or the top 12 reshuffling. Those are later rulings standing on top of this one, which is what the header of scripts/receipts.ts says a receipt records.
